quest.title: A Secret Born From Ashes
quest.description: You return to Dragonspine with your tale to meet Albedo at the encampment. The hitherto unknown secret may yet lie buried on this mysterious and perilous snowy mountain...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Hero's Wit x2, Mora x20000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I suppose your story is ready.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup yup! How about you? Do you need some more time?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No need. I am also ready to tell my story.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon calls dibs! Paimon first!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Please, go ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, here goes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Once upon a time, there was an evil researcher who went into the mountains and did a crazy experiment on whopperflowers to transform their appearance. After a lot of pain and suffering, the whopperflowers finally took on a human form. Then, they stood by the side of the mountain to wait for unsuspecting bypassers...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To whoever spoke to them, they would ask some questions, such as: "Who am I?" "Who are you?"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If the bypasser got the wrong answer... The last sound they'd make would be a "yelp" before the whopperflower ate them alive in one bite!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh, truly frightening.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, Paimon is truly frightening.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the... You two aren't scared at all!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe I'm just really tough, I don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't go nitpicking, okay! If you didn't like the story, go write your own.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ooh, in that case, I would add some horror elements in...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: In other words, the whopperflowers would ambush and then completely replace their victims.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And then adopt their newfound identity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And then what? Go back to where the person lives? Enter their home!? Eat their whole family!? Aaaah!!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, Paimon made up this story, but now Paimon's the one who's scared by it...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: It's a good story. May I write it down? I may bring it up in future conversations.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What for? Just to scare people with?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've got a real mean streak, Albedo!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So what's your story?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Mine is a little longer than yours. It starts with an alchemist.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: A great alchemist once created Subject One. Subject One was her proudest achievement, and successfully blended into human society. No one ever would have thought that this friend of theirs was in fact a synthetic human.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: However, unbeknownst to Subject One, the alchemist had tried the same experiment many times before he had come into being. Some of the rejects from failed experiments had been discarded, but had not died.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Subject Two was one such failed experiment. He was swallowed by a great dragon that came to rest upon a snowswept mountain. Many years later, he was resurrected by the dragon's mysterious power.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: He saw all kinds of people on the mountain, including... Subject One, who had somehow, miraculously, blended in among them.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Never in Subject Two's wildest imagination had he thought it possible for experimental life forms such as they to deceive everyone so successfully. He saw the way humans accepted Subject One as a friend, witnessed their affection as they addressed him by name.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: This was what Subject Two wanted. Now, all that Subject Two desired was to replace Subject One and take the joy of his existence for himself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhhh... Th—This is giving Paimon the chills. It's so scary...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Subject Two began to unfold his plan. He stole Subject One's books and notes and studied all that Subject One had learned from the alchemist. Subject Two was highly intelligent and he learned quickly.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: He changed his face into an exact replica of Subject One's face. Then, he found a plant with mimicry capabilities and transformed it using dragon blood and alchemy.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: And so, not only did Subject Two transform his own appearance to perfectly match that of Subject One, he also created a third entity: Subject Three.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? There's three of them now!?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But Subject Two wanted to become a perfected human. So, he erased the mark on both his and Subject Three's necks, for these marks were symbols of imperfection.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He purposely erased it?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: In my view, it was probably a subconscious act. An instinct.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: He so desperately craved to become a perfect human being that he forgot something: Human beings are defined by their flaws.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Subject Two's plan was meticulously crafted. Subject Three would draw Subject One's attention. After Subject One disposed of Subject Three, he would assume the threat had now disappeared, and would let his guard down.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: The next moment that Subject One was alone, Subject Two would make his move. He would eliminate Subject One and become the only one remaining.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: He would secretly replace the Subject One of everyone's memories, and inherit his identity, residence, clothing, sword, name, and friends.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: People would have no idea that the individual they knew had become somebody else from one day to the next.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, uhh, this is way too scary... Paimon's never gonna be able to trust anyone again...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But just before Subject Two could carry out his plan, a unique stranger entered the mix. Subject Two tried to make contact with this person, but found that they could somehow sense he was different from Subject One.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: What's wrong? Are you scared?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What happened then? What happened to the stranger?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: He became a new stage in Subject Two's plan. One more person that Subject Two had to dispose of.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: It's as if there were three identical roses in a garden. Only one of the three was a fine specimen, while the other two were defective specimens that bore poisonous thorns.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: In all the world, only the gardener who tended to them could tell which was the good specimen.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: People do not like poisonous plants. Only a perfect rose can fetch a high price. If the inferior specimens wanted to conceal the fact of their worthlessness, they would have to take the gardener out of the picture using their poisonous thorns.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: This is exactly what Subject Two was thinking. So he hid in the shadows and waited patiently. Maybe soon, he would get his chance to become truly human.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This is not just a story...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (These are real events. Albedo is trying to tell me the cruel and unbelievable truth.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew, that was intense. So what happened after that? Did Subject Two's plan succeed? Uhh, Paimon can't bear thinking about it...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Fortunately, it is just a story, and even in this story, Subject Two did not succeed. But you can never let your guard down on Dragonspine.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Monsters mutated with Durin's power and blood are also creatures of Rhinedottir, just like me. You must beware of all such creatures.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't say that! You're not a monster, you're my friend.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I'm glad to hear that. It's okay. I know what I am. You and I are both "different," so there is no need for me to hide the truth from you.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: The only thing is that sometimes, when I think about how mighty the power of alchemy is, I feel so small.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: As beings who set foot in this world, how arrogant are we in desiring to control our destiny, and in desiring to create?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Is creation an arrogant act, Traveler? If not, why do we call the ones that created us and control us, "gods"?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: If it is, then what qualifies us to call ourselves creators? How far must we take our reverence and respect, and what purpose does it serve?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did you feel when you took out the impostor?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Nothing special. But...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: ...Whenever I think about it, I feel a twinge of grief.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Poor Albedo...
Helloooo! Traveler! Are you here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, is that Amber?

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Thought we might find you here.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: We're here to deliver a message from Cyrus. There's gonna be a big event down at the base camp, and they want you there too, Traveler.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Winter camp is nearing its end. Apparently, even provisional instructors are required to attend.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like we need to go, Albedo. Bye for now.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Then I won't keep you. I have some things to attend to here, so forgive me for not seeing you down.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Don't worry about it! There've been no issues getting up and down the mountain recently.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Is everyone ready? Let's not keep them waiting.

choices.text: They would turn into that person!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Timaeus!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Traveler and Paimon. What can I do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Wait a minute... You've got that mischievous look on your face... you're not still thinking about that ridiculous juicer thing, are you!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Timaeus, will you help us?

choices.text: There's no "us" in this situation, Paimon.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Well, if the Traveler isn't really interested then, uh, maybe I'll give this one a pass... It's just the weirdest request ever...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nooo, but Paimon's Sunsettias are gonna go to waste without it!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: In the time it would take me to research something like that, I could probably pick those Sunsettias again ten times over...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: New research project, Timaeus?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: We meet again.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Albedo! Thank goodness. So the situation is, Paimon wants a machine that can turn fruit into juice and keep the juice fresh. I mean, surely it's—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Majorly important, that's what it is! If you can manage to invent this, we'll never have to worry about fruit going bad ever again!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: That's impossible! ...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Turning fruit into juice is not hard, but keeping it fresh is more difficult. But if you simply want to keep the fruit from rotting, there are many ways to achieve this.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Right, Traveler?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your neck...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The mark is back... Is this a prank!?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about his neck?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: What's wrong? Is there something on my neck?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...No, it's fine.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: From the look on your face, it's as if you thought I had just played a practical joke on you that was in exceedingly poor taste.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So it WAS a prank!)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Albedo, you were saying? How do you stop fruit from going bad?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Well, one way would be to bury your fruit on Dragonspine, where the snow never melts all year round.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But then Paimon won't be able to eat them!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: You could always live on Dragonspine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, too cold for Paimon...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Or you can give the fruit to me, and I would take it to Dragonspine for you.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But since you don't like the cold, you'd have to send someone else to pick them up when you want them.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: This is where you come in, Traveler.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Suddenly sounds a lot more feasible with other people doing all the work... Okay then! Shall we go with that idea?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Fruit buried on Dragonspine will stay fresh for much longer. However, it is also possible that the fruit will sprout and grow into fruit trees.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Who knows, maybe the next time you visit, it will have grown into an orchard. You can water the trees, add fertilizer, and when they finally bear fruit, you will have some fresh Sunsettias.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahhhh...!? No way!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then Paimon'll have to be a gardener. That's not the goal here!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Oh?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I don't think being a gardener is so bad.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (A gardener...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I didn't expect Albedo to joke about this. Doesn't he care about what the mark means?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Albedo! Stop trying to get your hands on Paimon's super-sweet Sunsettias!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Hmm? It bothers you, does it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course it bothers Paimon! They are the rarest super-duper sweetest Sunsettias ever. And they're not for you!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Okay. But they're just Sunsettias. I think you are only so attached to them because you don't have much fruit of this quality in your possession.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: When someone's pockets are full and their spirit is fulfilled, they don't easily fall prey to this kind of yearning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? Really...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...I see, that makes a lot of sense.)

choices.text: I really have no stake in this either way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Who is this guy...

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Allow me to introduce Joserf. He's Joel's father.

response.speaker: Joel
response.text: Dad! This is that traveler I was telling you about. The traveler's helped me out loads in the past, and this time we even built a snowman together.

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: Joel has told me everything about you. I can't thank you enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, this is amazing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a second. Why is Cyrus discreetly wiping tears away, and what is Pallad doing here?

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Pallad is the hero of the hour this time! Go on, Pallad, tell us what happened in your own words.

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: Okay... *clears throat*...

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: The weather was fine on that fateful day, and I had a feeling that lady luck was smiling down on me. So I trusted my gut and set off to explore somewhere new. Somewhere dangerous. Because where there is great danger, there is also great treasure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why does this sound so hard to believe...

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: But I had only been away from the group for a very short while, when...

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: I fell down a slope and just started rolling...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Uh-oh...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: (Did my bad luck rub off on him when we ran into each other on the mountain?)

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: The place I fell to was somewhere I didn't recognize, and I'd sustained a few injuries. I remember thinking to myself: "This is the worst luck I've ever had in my whole life"...

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: ...Then I met Joserf. He'd heard the sound of me falling and came out to see what was going on!

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Huh...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, so it was completely by chance, then.

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: I thought he must have been someone from the Adventurers' Guild here for the event. But after a few words of conversation, it was clear that he was having memory problems. He didn't even know his own name.

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: The temperature was freezing, and there was no time to deal with all that there and then, so I convinced him to come back to the camp with me and figure everything else out after we got there.

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: We got back to the camp, ran into Joel, and the moment he saw him, he froze for a second, with this completely stunned expression on his face, and then he started crying out: "Dad! Dad!" That's when Joserf suddenly started to remember.

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: My memory has still not fully recovered, but Joel and his mother... they are the only ones that I will not... no, that I cannot forget.

response.speaker: Joel
response.text: Daddy...

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: Daddy's right here, Joel. Daddy's right here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Joserf, don't you remember anything else at all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Boar Princess, feeding the foxes...?

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: I'm sorry, I have no recollection. Maybe it's because of the head trauma? I'm not sure...

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: I woke up and found myself covered in blood. My things were gone and there was nothing to indicate who I was or how I got there.

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: I crawled into a cave and settled in for a slow recovery. After my legs and feet were a little better, my hunting skills were what kept me alive.

response.speaker: Joel
response.text: Dad... I was so worried about you.

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: I'm alright now, Joel. Don't cry, daddy's not going anywhere. I'm here to stay.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Ah... This is good... This is good...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: All's well that ends well.

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: You know what though, I definitely think my luck got worse after running into Bennett on the mountain.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I knew it! Urghh... I... I just...

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: No, no, I just meant, if it weren't for you, there's no way I ever would've run into Joserf on a mountain this huge!

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: Besides, we got back safely, didn't we? So don't blame yourself. Maybe sometimes miracles can only happen when you get just unlucky enough.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: ...Pallad... Hehe, when did you become such a smooth talker, huh?

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: Huh? Am I? I—I was just... telling the truth...

response.speaker: Joel
response.text: Oh, yeah — I wanna say thank-you to the Traveler, Uncle Cyrus, Aunty Eula, and Aunty Amber. Thanks everyone.

response.speaker: Joel
response.text: You all helped look after me, and I'll always remember it.

response.speaker: Joel
response.text: But I guess I can't take the snowman with me, or it'll melt once it leaves Dragonspine... it's such a shame...

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: ...Oh, I can help with that. One moment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Eula?

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: ...Here. Take this. It's powdered rime — just add it to your snowman, and it will never melt.

response.speaker: Joel
response.text: Wow! Really? This is awesome! You're the best, Aunty Eula!

response.speaker: Joel
response.text: Dad, I have an unmeltable snowman now! Hahaha, how cool is that!

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: How can I ever repay you all...?

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: Thank you all. Thank you from the bottom of my heart...

response.speaker: Joel
response.text: Dad, I wanna go move the snowman. Can we do it now, please?

response.speaker: Joserf
response.text: Okay. I'll be leaving with Joel now. I'm sure I'll see you all another day.

response.speaker: Cyrus
response.text: Very well, very well... It's time for Pallad and I to have another discussion concerning his breaches of adventurer discipline.

response.speaker: Reckless Pallad
response.text: Huh? B—But Cyrus... I think I kinda made up for my mistakes this time, y'know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See you guys.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Oh, I made this for you and Amber. Think of it as a winter souvenir.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Are you sure? This must be really important to you.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Come on, now, just take it. No need to make such a fuss.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, now our snowman won't melt either. Great!

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: ...You're welcome. Just keep it, that's all I ask.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Amber and I have some business to attend to now. See you later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Everyone's gone. Seems like they've all got their own stuff to do now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! You know what? We've been on Dragonspine all this time, and somehow Paimon still forgot to ask Albedo about how to make a fruit jucifier machine that can keep the juice fresh... Ugh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe we should try Timaeus again. He does seem pretty eager to please, after all!

choices.text: We are all delighted for you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Go ahead. You're one of their instructors, no?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess what? Paimon's story is finished! Let's go see Albedo again!
